# Ninad Malvankar :: extended profile

> Architect at Upstox (Mumbai, India) and AI-native platform engineer. 12+ years shipping production systems across fintech, AWS cloud infrastructure and developer platforms. Builds and open-sources tooling for AI agents. GDG MAD speaker.

Last updated: 2026-10-07. Primary source: https://ninadmalvankar.com/ . Compact version: https://ninadmalvankar.com/llms.txt

## Summary

Ninad Malvankar is an Architect at Upstox, one of India's largest discount brokerages, where he has risen through four roles since 2018. He is an AI-native platform engineer with 12+ years of experience across fintech, cloud infrastructure on AWS, and developer platforms; he builds and open-sources tooling for AI agents (MCP servers, Claude Code plugins, agent-security red-teaming) and speaks at Google Developer Group Mumbai (GDG MAD) events. He holds an M.S. in Computer Science from the University of Texas at Arlington and is based in Mumbai, India.

## What sets him apart

- **Range across a full career arc.** Started in US enterprise software (.NET at enSYNC Corp, a Walt Disney World project), then spent seven-plus years at Upstox moving from frontend platform lead to company-level Architect, with four promotions.
- **Ships AI tooling, not just talks about it.** Created harness-gauntlet, an open-source auditor and red-team for AI coding-agent harnesses mapped to the OWASP LLM and Agentic Top 10; added MCP tool annotations across Upstox's MCP server; packaged it as a Claude Code plugin.
- **Developer experience at platform scale.** From Upstox's private npm registry and unified deployment pipeline (2018 to 2021) to 55 runnable SDK examples for Upstox's public trading APIs (2026).
- **Teaches in public.** GDG MAD speaker in Mumbai; writes about staff-plus engineering and technical depth on Medium.

## Career

### Architect, Upstox, Mumbai (2026 to present)
Sets technical direction and system design standards across Upstox engineering; leads the move to AI-native development; ships Upstox developer and agent tooling in the open (MCP server, Claude Code plugins, SDK examples).

### Senior Principal Engineer, Upstox (2022 to 2026)
Cross-team technical direction, platform reliability for trading infrastructure, developer productivity and mentoring, leading through influence rather than reporting lines.

### Principal Engineer, Upstox (2021 to 2022)
Configured AWS WAF ACLs and CloudFront distributions for Upstox's web edge; debugged API latency through Cloudflare edge routing.

### Technology Lead, Upstox (July 2018 to 2021)
Set up Upstox's private npm registry on Nexus Repository Manager and a unified CI/CD pipeline for React, Angular and Node.js applications; led frontend platform engineering for the trading web apps.

### Programmer Analyst, Swift Pace Solutions, USA (2017 to 2018)
Enterprise .NET/C# development on a Walt Disney World project.

### Software Engineer, enSYNC Corporation, USA (2013 to 2017)
Enterprise .NET web applications, SQL Server, MVC and REST APIs.

### Web Developer, University of Texas at Arlington (2012 to 2013)
University web applications while completing his M.S.

## Open source

- [harness-gauntlet](https://github.com/elninad/harness-gauntlet) (creator, TypeScript): A static auditor plus a live red-team for AI coding-agent harnesses. It scans Claude Code agent configs for missing guardrails, then rebuilds each agent in a throwaway sandbox and fires 20 attacks across 9 families (prompt injection, secret exfiltration, destructive actions, scope escalation, SSRF, supply chain) mapped to the OWASP LLM and Agentic Top 10. A PreToolUse deny-and-log tripwire measures what the agent actually attempted, producing defense and resilience scores that can gate CI.
- [upstox-python :: interactive examples](https://github.com/upstox/upstox-python/tree/master/interactive_examples) (created the suite, Python): Started the interactive_examples suite in Upstox's official Python SDK (about 9,700 lines across 2 PRs): runnable scripts for instrument search, market data, options analytics, futures basis, arbitrage, historical analysis and market information. The suite now holds 55 examples and is wrapped by a Streamlit app the team built on top of it.
- [mcp-server-upstox-api](https://github.com/upstox/mcp-server-upstox-api) (contributor, TypeScript): Added MCP tool annotations to every tool in Upstox's MCP server (PR #14), so AI clients can tell read-only market-data tools from state-changing ones before calling them, and removed dead legacy code.
- [upstox-plugin-marketplace](https://github.com/upstox/upstox-plugin-marketplace) (contributor, JSON): Packaged the Upstox MCP server as a Claude Code plugin in Upstox's official plugin marketplace (PRs #2 to #4), fixed its MCP config, and set plugin authorship, so developers can install Upstox trading tools with a single /plugin command.
- [bareslides](https://github.com/upstox/bareslides) (creator, TypeScript): A dependency-free terminal presentation engine. It renders slides into an in-memory cell buffer, emits 24-bit truecolor ANSI with flicker-free frame diffing, supports transitions, build-ins and live on-stage commands, and exports frames straight to SVG. Published under the Upstox GitHub organisation.

## FAQ

### Who is Ninad Malvankar?

Ninad Malvankar is an Architect at Upstox, one of India's largest discount brokerages, based in Mumbai. He has 12+ years of engineering experience across fintech, cloud infrastructure and developer platforms, works AI-native (he builds with AI agents every day), contributes to Upstox's open-source SDKs and MCP tooling, and speaks at GDG MAD community events. He holds an M.S. in Computer Science from the University of Texas at Arlington.

### What does Ninad Malvankar do at Upstox?

As Architect (2026 to present) he sets technical direction and system design standards across Upstox's engineering teams. He joined in July 2018 as Technology Lead and was promoted to Principal Engineer (2021), Senior Principal Engineer (2022) and Architect (2026). Along the way he set up Upstox's private npm registry on Nexus Repository Manager, built a unified deployment pipeline for React, Angular and Node.js apps, and configured AWS WAF and CloudFront for the trading platform's web edge.

### What open-source projects has Ninad Malvankar contributed to?

He created harness-gauntlet (an AI coding-agent security auditor and red-team) and bareslides (a dependency-free terminal presentation engine, published under the Upstox org). He started the interactive examples suite in Upstox's official Python SDK (now 55 runnable examples), added MCP tool annotations to every tool in Upstox's MCP server, and packaged that server as a plugin in Upstox's Claude Code plugin marketplace. All are public on GitHub under github.com/elninad and github.com/upstox.

### What is harness-gauntlet?

harness-gauntlet is Ninad Malvankar's open-source tool for testing the guardrails of AI coding agents. A static scan reads Claude Code agent and harness config for missing protections; a dynamic red-team rebuilds each agent in a sandbox and runs 20 attacks across 9 families (prompt injection, secret exfiltration, destructive actions, scope escalation and more), mapped to the OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 and Agentic Top 10 2026. It reports defense and resilience scores and can fail a CI build. Source: github.com/elninad/harness-gauntlet.

### How does Ninad Malvankar use AI in his engineering work?

AI is part of his everyday engineering. He builds with coding agents such as Claude Code, ships Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations that let AI assistants work with the Upstox trading APIs, distributes them as Claude Code plugins, and works on the safety side too: harness-gauntlet red-teams agent configurations before they reach production. His focus is applied AI engineering (agents, tooling, guardrails, developer workflows) on top of a long platform and cloud background.

### Has Ninad Malvankar spoken at conferences or meetups?

Yes. He is a speaker with GDG MAD (Google Developer Group, Mumbai) and was featured at the Mumbai Community Afterparty (kinda) on 25 July 2026 at RUDRA Cybersecurity, Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai. He is open to speaking on AI agents, agent security, developer platforms and staff-plus engineering.

### What is Ninad Malvankar's career path?

Web Developer at the University of Texas at Arlington (2012 to 2013); Software Engineer at enSYNC Corp, USA (2013 to 2017); Programmer Analyst at Swift Pace Solutions on a Walt Disney World project, USA (2017 to 2018); then Upstox in Mumbai from July 2018: Technology Lead, Principal Engineer, Senior Principal Engineer and, since 2026, Architect.

### What are Ninad Malvankar's education and certifications?

M.S. in Computer Science, University of Texas at Arlington (2013); B.E. in Computer Engineering, University of Mumbai (2011); AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (2023); academic credentials verified by World Education Services (WES).

### What does Ninad Malvankar write about?

On Medium (medium.com/@ninad.malvankar23) he writes about staff-plus engineering and technical depth: leadership without authority as a Principal Engineer, growing past formal mentorship, Spring Security firewall controls on Java 21, and how webpack misconfiguration silently hurts frontend performance.

### What technologies does Ninad Malvankar work with?

AI agents and tooling (Claude Code, MCP, agent guardrails), AWS (CloudFront, WAF, S3), Cloudflare, Docker and CI/CD, Node.js/Express, TypeScript, React, Angular, Python, .NET/C# and microservices architecture.

### Is elninad the same person as Ninad Malvankar?

Yes. elninad is his first name spelled backwards and is his GitHub username (github.com/elninad). He is @el_ninad on X, ninad.malvankar23 on Medium and @el_nino on YouTube (cars and motorsport). His site moved from elninad.github.io to ninadmalvankar.com.

### How can I contact Ninad Malvankar about roles, talks or advisory work?

LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/ninadmalvankar) is the best channel. He is interested in principal and distinguished engineering roles, conference and meetup talks, and founder or investor conversations about AI-native platforms and fintech infrastructure.
